text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract survived a test of support at 93.470, but the market is looking slightly vulnerable after slipping through a one-month rising trendline.
*Local T-bond tender result at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).

The September Australian 10-year bond futures contract survived several tests of 93.470 support, but the market is looking slightly vulnerable after slipping through a one-month steep rising trendline.
The contract ended SYCOM trading at 93.505, up from Monday's 93.475 pit close.

The market gleened support from a firm, albeit thinly traded, U.S. Treasury market, but as the local debt futures have a 50 basis point monetary policy easing priced in, upside potential is expected to be limited until such an event becomes a reality, analysts said.

While the local 10-year contract has breached a one-month rising trendline, at current levels it remains well above the broader treadline running since early April, which currently stands at around 93.000.

The domestic market sees the June trade balance of goods and services at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), although the figure will be distorted by the Reserve Bank's recent gold sales, which has made forecasting the outcome fairly difficult.
Meanwhile, final bids for a A$500 million two-tranche bond tender, the first of the 1997/98 fiscal year, are due at 12.45 p.m. (0245 GMT) and the result will be 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).

U.S. Treasuries rallied after the Treasury department said that it expected a net market borrowing requirement for the third quarter of US$10 billion, about half of what U.S. analysts had expected, and in anticipation of a friendly second quarter employment cost index later on Tuesday.
